I’m 57 this year, and I’ve been working these 14 mu in Quzhou for 20 years. I only finished primary school, but I know my land. I don’t need books to tell me what works—I watch my own fields, and I watch the neighbors who do well.

My main crop is cotton, and I put 8 mu into it. Last year I got about 700 jin of seed cotton per mu, and this year I’m planting hybrid Bt cotton again, the kind from the county seed dealer that resists bollworm. My neighbor Lao Zhang tried a new hybrid last year and got maybe 50 jin more per mu, so I’m buying that same one. Before planting in late April, I rotary till the ground to break it up. For base fertilizer I spread half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu—that’s a 50-jin bag for every 2 mu. Then when the plants flower and again when the bolls set, I top-dress with urea, about 30 jin per mu total. I irrigate four times: planting water, early flowering, peak boll, and late boll. Well water costs electricity, but if the bolls dry up you lose everything. I spray pesticide five times—even Bt cotton gets aphids and red spider mites. I hire the village drone sprayer, 5 yuan per mu each time. I expect about 350 kg per mu of seed cotton if the weather holds.

The other 6 mu is in winter wheat, already in the ground from last October. Now it’s spring, so I spread 40 jin of urea per mu for the green-up fertilizer. I already put down base fertilizer last autumn, 50 jin of compound per mu. I irrigate twice—green-up water and jointing water. I spray once if I see rust or aphids. No tillage now, the wheat is already growing. Should get about 480 kg per mu.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I immediately put in summer maize on those same 6 mu. No time to waste—I rotary till quick and plant hybrid seeds, one bag covers about 3 mu. Base fertilizer is 50 jin of compound per mu, and at the big trumpet stage I top-dress with 25 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate twice if the summer turns dry, especially when the tassels come out. Two pesticide sprays for armyworm and corn borer. In a normal year that gives me 550 kg per mu.

I have 8 people in the house. Some work outside so we have cash coming in, but fertilizer is still expensive—urea is 120 yuan a bag, compound is about 160 yuan. I’d rather put a little too much fertilizer than risk losing yield. Last year Lao Wang tried to save 200 yuan on fertilizer and his cotton yield dropped by half. That was a hard lesson. I follow what worked before, I watch the neighbors, and I don’t take big risks.
